title: How steady is an average of 16 examples?
hook: One example gives a jittery step. How much calmer is an average of sixteen?

knows: that gradient descent steps along a slope estimated from data
doesNotKnow: that averaging b examples shrinks the noise in the step by the square root of b

misconception: Using one example per step is as reliable as using many.
objective: The learner can say that averaging a batch shrinks gradient noise by the square root of the batch size, so 16 times the work buys 4 times the steadiness.

claims.text: Toy setup: each example's gradient is the true slope 1 plus noise with sd 1; a step is the average over a batch; the stage shows 30 steps at each batch size (1, 4, 16, 64) and is labelled 'Toy: noise sd 1 per example'.
claims.source: Brief 53 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md; draws(), stepsAt() in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: In this toy the 30 steps spread with sd 1.18 at batch 1, 0.23 at batch 16 and 0.13 at batch 64 (measured on the stage; sample sd, n-1).
claims.source: Node re-run of Demo.tsx draws() with seed 11 (the first seed tried, not tuned): 1.183, 0.584 (batch 4), 0.226, 0.132. Other batches of 30 steps differ: this is one run.

claims.text: The standard error of an average of b independent values with sd 1 is 1/sqrt(b): 1, 0.25 and 0.125 for batches of 1, 16 and 64.
claims.source: Variance of a mean of b independent values is sigma^2/b. The brief's script (50,000 trials) gave 0.997 for batch 1 and 0.249 for batch 16.

claims.text: Across 2000 seeds, the sd of 30 steps at batch 16 ran from 0.20 to 0.30 (5th to 95th percentile; median 0.25).
claims.source: Node re-run over seeds 1 to 2000 with the same generator: p5 0.195, median 0.248, p95 0.303.

claims.text: 16 times the work (examples per step) buys 4 times the steadiness (noise sd divided by 4).
claims.source: sqrt(16) = 4. For real minibatch SGD, see Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville 2016, Deep Learning, section 8.1.3 (the standard error of the mean falls as 1/sqrt(n)); real gradient noise is not exactly independent with sd 1.

recall.question: A training step averages the gradients of 100 examples instead of 25 (four times the work), and each example's gradient has the same noise. The step's noise is about:
recall.why: Noise in an average falls as 1 over the square root of the batch size: 4 times the examples halves the noise.
